description: Book key test vectors for Casebound position sync (format 1). The key is fileName.precomposedStringWithCanonicalMapping.lowercased() + "|" + String(fileSizeBytes): the file name only (with extension, no folders), Unicode NFC first, then Swift's String.lowercased(), then a pipe and the size in bytes as a base-10 integer. expectedKey values were produced by Swift on macOS and are the reference. The *Scalars fields spell every non-ASCII scalar as \u{hex} so NFC and NFD names can be told apart.
dotnetNote: The Windows app should compute Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormC) then ToLowerInvariant() and compare against expectedKey. Vectors marked dotnetMayDiffer are the known risks: .NET invariant lowercasing is one-to-one per UTF-16 unit (simple case mapping), while Swift's lowercased() applies full Unicode mappings, so U+0130 (I with dot) becomes two scalars in Swift. Newer scripts such as Georgian Mtavruli depend on each side's Unicode case tables. A mismatch only means that one book's position won't sync between Windows and Apple devices; nothing else breaks.

vectors.note: Real fixture: matches the key CHEWBACCA (Windows) already wrote for this book.
Real fixture from the shared Audiobooks folder.
Extension is part of the key and is lowercased too.
NFC: e-acute as one scalar U+00E9.
NFD: e + U+0301. Must produce the SAME key as the NFC vector above (normalize to NFC before lowercasing).
NFD with three combining marks; composes to U+00E8, U+00FB, U+00E9.
Hangul as conjoining jamo (NFD); NFC composes it to 3 syllables.
U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN: NFC maps it to U+00C5 before lowercasing, giving U+00E5.
U+212A KELVIN SIGN: NFC maps it to ASCII K, then k.

U+0130 capital I with dot above. Swift lowercased() uses the FULL Unicode mapping and yields TWO scalars: i + U+0307. .NET ToLowerInvariant() uses simple one-to-one mapping and yields either U+0069 or leaves U+0130 unchanged depending on runtime/ICU mode, so the key will likely differ. Dotless i (U+0131) is already lowercase in both.
ASCII I lowercases to ASCII i in both (neither side is Turkish-culture aware).
U+00DF sharp s is already lowercase; unchanged in both. (Uppercasing would differ, lowercasing does not.)
U+1E9E capital sharp s lowercases to U+00DF in both (simple mapping exists).
Emoji (astral plane, surrogate pairs in UTF-16) and a flag sequence pass through unchanged.

Greek capitals ending in SIGMA. Swift lowercased() does NOT apply the word-final sigma rule: every U+03A3 becomes U+03C3, the same as .NET ToLowerInvariant. Context-sensitive lowercasers (Python str.lower, ICU full mapping, JavaScript) give a final U+03C2 instead, so do not use those.
U+01C4 DZ-caron digraph lowercases to U+01C6.
Fullwidth Latin: U+FF26 and U+FF37 lowercase to U+FF46 and U+FF57. NFC does not fold width.
Georgian Mtavruli capitals (Unicode 11, 2018). Needs Unicode 11+ case data on both sides; an older .NET/Windows Unicode table leaves them unchanged.
Zero-byte size still appends |0.
Size above 2^32: must be a 64-bit integer on Windows (long, not int).
Spaces and punctuation are kept as-is; only case changes.
